definition_zh: 恐怖；恐惧；可怕的人或事物；恐怖行动
definition_en: a feeling of extreme fear, the use of violence to frighten people, or a person or thing that causes great fear
core_image: 深夜空巷里身后逼近的脚步声：心跳到喉咙口的那种怕
scene: 停电的楼道一片漆黑，身后传来急促的脚步声。She froze in terror as the footsteps came closer.
sceneCN: 这里 terror 是「极度恐惧」（第 1 个义项：强烈的恐惧感）；句意：脚步声逼近，她吓得僵在原地。

pos.zh: 恐怖；恐惧；可怕的人或事；恐怖行动

collocations.zh: 班里的捣蛋鬼；令人生畏者

derivatives.zh: 恐怖分子（由 terror 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，指实施恐怖活动的人）
使恐惧；使害怕（由 terror 加动词后缀派生，义为把恐惧灌进人心）
令人恐惧的（terrify 的现在分词转形容词）
吓坏了的（terrify 的过去分词转形容词）

senses.title: Extreme fear
senses.definition: the state of feeling extreme and overwhelming fear
senses.definitionCN: 感到强烈而压倒性的恐惧的状态
senses.example: The villagers fled in terror when the flood came.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水来时村民惊恐地逃散。
senses.why: The word names fear at its highest pitch, when the body reacts before the mind can decide.
senses.whyCN: 它命名的是恐惧的最高强度：身体先于头脑作出反应的那一瞬。

senses.title: Violence used to frighten people
senses.titleCN: 恐怖行径：以暴力制造恐慌
senses.definition: the deliberate use of violence and fear to control people
senses.definitionCN: 刻意使用暴力与恐惧来控制人群
senses.example: The dictator ruled the country by a campaign of terror.
senses.exampleCN: 独裁者靠恐怖统治控制这个国家。
senses.why: Fear can be weaponized: when fright is produced on purpose, the feeling itself becomes a method of ruling.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧可以被武器化：当恐惧被刻意制造，这种感觉本身就变成了统治手段。

senses.title: A person or thing that causes fear
senses.definition: a person or thing that frightens others greatly
senses.definitionCN: 让别人非常害怕的人或事物
senses.example: Her elder brother is a terror behind the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥开车是个马路杀手。
senses.why: Whatever reliably produces the feeling can be called by it: the cause borrows the name of the effect.
senses.whyCN: 凡是可靠地制造恐惧的东西都可以借用它的名字：原因借走了结果的名称。

senses.title: A frightening or troublesome child
senses.definition: a child who behaves badly and is difficult to handle, often said with affection
senses.definitionCN: 胡闹难管的孩子，常带亲昵口吻
senses.example: Young Tommy is a little terror at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 小汤米在饭桌上是个小捣蛋。
senses.why: The effect produced is chaos rather than fear, but the fixed phrase keeps the name, softened by smiles.
senses.whyCN: 制造的效果是混乱而非害怕，但固定短语保留了这个名字，且被笑意软化了。

intro.en: Terror is a Latin loan: the noun terrere meant to frighten, and terror was the fright itself. English took the word through French and never lost the ancient image.
intro.cn: terror 是拉丁语借词：动词 terrere 意为「吓」，名词 terror 就是那股吓意。英语经法语接收了这个词，古老的意象从未丢失。

items.en: The Latin verb terrere meant to frighten or make tremble, and terror named the state of being frightened.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 terrere 意为惊吓、使人发抖，名词 terror 指被吓住的状态。

items.en: The root tremble-image links terror to the idea that real fear shakes the body visibly.
items.cn: 词根的「发抖」意象把 terror 与「真正的恐惧会看得见地摇动身体」联系在一起。

items.en: French carried terreur into medieval and early modern writing, keeping both private dread and public violence.
items.cn: 法语把 terreur 带进中世纪与近代早期的文字，既有私人的惧怕，也有公共的暴力。

items.en: English borrowed terror in the late Middle Ages, at first for religious dread and bodily shaking before God.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入 terror，最初用于宗教性的敬畏与在神面前发抖。

items.en: The Reign of Terror in the 1790s fixed the political sense, and later everyday use softened it to pranks and mischievous children.
items.cn: 1790 年代的恐怖统治固定了政治义；此后日常用法又把它软化，用来称呼恶作剧的孩子。

note.en: Terror sits beside its own verb and agent, and beside fear words of different strength.
note.cn: terror 与它自己的动词、施动者并列，也与强度不同的恐惧类词并列。

entries.definition: to fill someone with great fear; the verb form of the terror family
entries.definitionCN: 使人大为恐惧；terror 词族的动词形式

entries.definition: originally frightening, now excellent; the old sense of terror survives only in the spelling
entries.definitionCN: 原义吓人，今义极好；terror 的古义只残留在拼写里

entries.definition: a small hunting dog; only looks close to terror, etymology is different
entries.definitionCN: 一种小型猎犬；只是拼写接近 terror，词源不同

entries.definition: fear mixed with anticipation, a slower and heavier feeling than terror
entries.definitionCN: 带着预期的恐惧，比 terror 更慢更沉

entries.definition: sudden wild fear that spreads in a crowd and destroys self-control
entries.definitionCN: 人群中蔓延、让人失去自控的突发恐慌

entries.definition: fear mixed with disgust or shock at something repulsive
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧中混着厌恶或震惊；对可怖之物的反应

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin verb terrere, the terrify family, the Reign of Terror, and the schoolroom little terror.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁动词 terrere、terrify 词族、恐怖统治、以及教室里的小捣蛋。

normal.en: Terrere in Latin means to make someone tremble; terror is fear that shakes the body.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 terrere 意为使人发抖；terror 就是会摇动身体的恐惧。

normal.en: Terrify, terrified and terrifying all carry the same root into verbs and adjectives.
normal.cn: terrify、terrified、terrifying 把同一词根带进动词与形容词。

normal.en: The Reign of Terror in history fixed the sense of violence used as government.
normal.cn: 历史上的恐怖统治固定了「以暴力为统治」的义项。

normal.en: Strike terror into the enemy: aim the fear like an arrow.
normal.cn: strike terror into the enemy：像箭一样把恐惧射进敌心。

normal.en: A little terror at home frightens nobody; the phrase only borrows the word for mischief.
normal.cn: 家里的「小 terror」谁也吓不倒；短语只是借这个词来称呼淘气。

abstract.en: Terror is the moment the body votes before the mind has finished counting.
abstract.cn: terror 是身体在头脑尚未数完票之前就先投票的那一刻。

abstract.en: Fear as a tool of power turns a feeling into a wall.
abstract.cn: 被当作权力的工具时，恐惧就成了一堵墙。

abstract.en: A shaking hand can be afraid, and can also be the thing that frightens others.
abstract.cn: 发抖的手可以是在害怕，也可以正是吓坏别人的东西。

examples.en: She fled the burning house in terror.
examples.cn: 她惊恐地逃离着火的房子。

examples.en: The bomb exploded with a terror that nobody in the street had known before.
examples.cn: 炸弹爆炸带来街上无人经历过的恐怖。

examples.en: Visiting the dentist terrified him as a child.
examples.cn: 小时候看牙医吓坏了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太怕」——太怕了，腿直发抖 → terror 恐怖、恐惧

root: 拉丁语 terrere「惊吓、使发抖」→ 拉丁名词 terror「恐惧」→ 经法语进入英语；terrify、terrific、terrier 一带词形相近但义路各异。

sensesIntro.en: Terror begins as pure fear at its strongest, then stretches into fear as a weapon, the frightful cause itself, and finally the smiling sense of a mischievous child.
sensesIntro.cn: terror 从最高强度的恐惧出发，延伸为作为武器的恐惧、可怕的原因本身，最后软化为淘气孩子的昵称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fear so strong the body trembles before the mind decides.
core.cn: 核心意象：强烈到身体先于头脑发抖的恐惧。

branches.en: The feeling at its highest pitch.
branches.cn: 恐惧的最高强度。

branches.en: Fear produced on purpose becomes a method of control.
branches.cn: 被刻意制造的恐惧成为统治手段。

branches.en: The cause borrows the name of the feeling it creates.
branches.cn: 原因借走它所制造的 feelings 的名称。

branches.en: Everyday speech softens the word to playful mischief.
branches.cn: 日常口语把这个词软化成顽皮的昵称。

branches.en: Private trembling and public violence are one root apart.
branches.cn: 私人的发抖与公共的暴力只隔一个词根。

intro.en: Terror builds its family with the agent suffix -ist, the verb suffixes -ify and -able, and the noun suffix -ism.
intro.cn: terror 用表人后缀 -ist、动词后缀 -ify 与 -able、名词后缀 -ism 构建词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gave English terror directly; terrere is also the source of terrific and the French-derived detour behind deter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语直接把 terror 交给英语；terrere 同样派生 terrific，也绕经法语造出 deter。

items.meaning: a person who uses terror as a political weapon
items.meaningCN: 以恐怖为政治武器的人
items.example: The terrorist group claimed the attack.
items.exampleCN: 恐怖组织宣称对袭击负责。

items.meaning: to fill someone with great fear
items.example: The horror film terrified the children.
a terrifying noise in the dark
He was terrified of dogs.

items.meaning: to control people by repeated terror
items.meaningCN: 以持续的恐怖手段控制
items.example: The gang terrorized the whole street.
items.exampleCN: 这伙匪帮恐吓了整条街的人。

items.example: High fines deter careless drivers.
items.exampleCN: 高额罚款让粗心的司机却步。

items.example: The alarm is a good deterrent to thieves.
items.exampleCN: 警报器是很好的防盗威慑。

items.meaning: a small secret group of terrorists
items.example: Police broke up a terror cell in the port.
items.exampleCN: 警方捣毁了港口的一个恐怖小组。

items.meaning: a glass case for growing plants
items.example: The school keeps a terrarium of ferns.

definition_zh: 恐怖分子；恐怖主义者；恐怖主义的
definition_en: a person who uses violence and fear for political ends, or relating to such violence
core_image: 把恐惧当武器的人：藏在人群里，让所有人不敢安心生活
scene: 警报响起时，整座车站的人都在往外跑。The police sealed the exits to search for the terrorist.
sceneCN: 这里 terrorist 是「恐怖分子」（第 1 个义项：以暴力制造恐惧来达到政治目的的人）；句意：警方封锁出口搜捕恐怖分子。

pos.zh: 恐怖主义的；与恐怖活动有关的

derivatives.zh: 恐怖；恐惧（terrorist 的基础词，指强烈的恐惧本身）
恐怖主义（由 terrorist 去掉表人后缀改加 -ism，指整套恐怖手段与思想）
恐吓；以恐怖手段控制（terror 加动词后缀构成）
反恐；反恐怖主义（counter- 加 terrorism，指对抗恐怖的行动）

senses.title: A person using fear for political aims
senses.definition: a person who deliberately uses violence against civilians to achieve political goals
senses.definitionCN: 为达到政治目的而蓄意对平民使用暴力的人
senses.example: A terrorist planted the bomb near the embassy.
senses.exampleCN: 一名恐怖分子在大使馆附近安放了炸弹。
senses.why: The agent suffix -ist names the person who practises terror; the defining trait is civilians as targets and politics as motive.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 点名了「施行恐怖的人」；其定义特征是：目标为平民，动机为政治。

senses.title: The adjective of such violence
senses.definition: relating to or characteristic of terrorism or terrorists
senses.definitionCN: 与恐怖主义或恐怖分子有关的
senses.example: The city tightened terrorist alert levels after the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 警告发出后，全市上调了恐怖活动警戒级别。
senses.why: Once the person is named, the name slides onto the acts and the alert levels connected with him.
senses.whyCN: 人被命名之后，名称就会滑向他所作的行径及与之相连的警戒状态。

senses.title: A member labelled by a viewpoint
senses.titleCN: （因立场不同而被称作的）恐怖分子
senses.definition: a person so described by one side in a conflict, since the same fighter may be called a freedom fighter by another
senses.definitionCN: 冲突一方对对方的称呼；同一战斗者可能被另一方称为自由战士
senses.example: One paper called him a terrorist, the other a hero of the resistance.
senses.exampleCN: 一家报纸称他为恐怖分子，另一家称他为抵抗英雄。
senses.why: The word carries judgement inside it, so history shows the same person wearing the label and losing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词内部自带评判，因此历史里同一个人会先戴上这标签、再被摘掉。

intro.en: Terrorist is terror plus the French agent suffix -iste. It was born in the 1790s, when the French Revolutionary government itself was described as governing by terror.
intro.cn: terrorist 是 terror 加法语表人后缀 -iste。它诞生于 1790 年代——当年法国革命政府正被描述为「以恐怖治国」。

items.en: Latin terror supplied the base: fear at its strongest, from terrere, to frighten.
items.cn: 拉丁名词 terror 提供了词基：最强度的恐惧，出自 terrere「惊吓」。

items.en: French terreur and the agent suffix -iste prepared the shape of the modern word.
items.cn: 法语 terreur 与表人后缀 -iste 塑出了现代词形。

items.en: In the 1790s the Reign of Terror made terror a tool of state; contemporaries spoke of its agents in government.
items.cn: 1790 年代的恐怖统治把恐怖变成国家工具；当时的人就谈到政府中的施行者。

items.en: English had taken terror through French in the late Middle Ages, first for religious dread.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期经法语借得 terror，最初用于宗教性的惧怕。

items.en: The 19th and 20th centuries narrowed terrorist to non-state violence against civilians, and terrorism named the method.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪把 terrorist 收窄为针对平民的非国家暴力，terrorism 则命名了这套手段。

note.en: The first group is the terror word family; the second compares labels for armed violence in politics.
note.cn: 第一组是 terror 词族；第二组比较政治语境中对武装暴力的不同称呼。

entries.definition: the system or practice of using terror; the -ism names the method, not the person
entries.definitionCN: 恐怖主义；-ism 指方法体系而非人

entries.definition: to frighten people repeatedly so as to control them
entries.definitionCN: 反复恐吓以控制他人

entries.definition: now excellent; originally frightening, from the same Latin root but a different sense path
entries.definitionCN: 今义极好；原义吓人，同一拉丁词根但义路不同

entries.definition: an irregular fighter; attacks military targets, unlike the terrorist who targets civilians
entries.definitionCN: 游击队员；袭击军事目标，不同于以平民为目标的恐怖分子

entries.definition: a person with radical views; may be violent or not, while terrorist is defined by violence
entries.definitionCN: 极端主义者；观点激进但不必然使用暴力

entries.definition: a combative member of a group; broader than terrorist and not always about violence against civilians
entries.definitionCN: 激进成员；比 terrorist 宽泛，不必然针对平民施暴

normalIntro.en: Real links: the -ist agent suffix, the terrorism -ism form, the 1790s origin, and the counter- opposite.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：-ist 表人后缀、terrorism 的 -ism 形式、1790 年代的起源、以及 counter- 反义构词。

normal.en: Terror + -ist: the -ist names the person who practises the fear.
normal.cn: terror + -ist：-ist 给「施行恐惧的人」命名。

normal.en: Terrorism with -ism is the method; terrorist with -ist is the doer.
normal.cn: 带 -ism 的 terrorism 是方法；带 -ist 的 terrorist 是行为者。

normal.en: The word was first used about a government that ruled by terror in the 1790s.
normal.cn: 这个词最初描述的是 1790 年代以恐怖治国的政府。

normal.en: Counter + terrorism gives counterterrorism, the fight against it.
normal.cn: counter + terrorism 得到 counterterrorism，即反恐。

normal.en: Guerrilla, extremist and terrorist differ in who they target and how.
normal.cn: guerrilla、extremist、terrorist 的区别在于打击对象与手段。

abstract.en: A name that decides, before any trial, who the enemy is.
abstract.cn: 一个在审判之前就判定谁是敌人的名字。

abstract.en: Fear aimed at the crowd is the weapon; the headline is only its sound.
abstract.cn: 瞄准人群的恐惧才是武器，标题只是它的声响。

abstract.en: Labels move with power: yesterday's terrorist can be tomorrow's statesman.
abstract.cn: 标签随权力移动：昨日的恐怖分子可以是明日的政治家。

examples.en: Terrorists attacked the subway during the morning rush.
examples.cn: 恐怖分子在早高峰袭击了地铁。

examples.en: New laws made it easier to prosecute terrorist suspects.
examples.cn: 新法律使起诉恐怖活动嫌疑人变得更容易。

examples.en: International terrorism changed airport security forever.
examples.cn: 国际恐怖主义永久性地改变了机场安检。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太怕入室」——太怕有人入室行凶，因为外面有恐怖分子 → terrorist 恐怖分子

root: 拉丁 terror（terrere「惊吓」的名词）+ 法语表人后缀 -iste → 英语 terrorist；词诞生于 1790 年代法国大革命语境。

sensesIntro.en: Terrorist names the person first, then transfers to the adjective, and finally shows its built-in judgement when labels clash in a conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: terrorist 先命名其人，再滑向形容词用法，最后在冲突双方的标签之争中显露其内置的评判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who turns fear itself into a weapon.
core.cn: 核心意象：把恐惧本身当作武器的人。

branches.en: The -ist suffix fixes the person who practises terror.
branches.cn: -ist 后缀锁定施行恐怖的人。

branches.en: The name spreads to the acts and alerts around the person.
branches.cn: 名称扩散到其行径与相关警戒。

branches.en: Whose side tells the word decides the label.
branches.cn: 立场决定标签归属。

branches.en: From person to policy: one suffix apart.
branches.cn: 从人到行径：只差一个后缀。

branches.en: History shows labels being pinned on and taken off.
branches.cn: 历史上标签被钉上又被摘下。

intro.en: Terrorist is built with the agent suffix -ist; the family adds -ism, -ize and the prefix counter-.
intro.cn: terrorist 用表人后缀 -ist 构成；词族还加上 -ism、-ize 与前缀 counter-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base terror sits under the whole family; Latin itself used terror simply for fear and for the frightener in religious language.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族建立在拉丁词基 terror 之上；拉丁语本身用 terror 指恐惧及宗教语言中的可怖之物。

items.meaning: a person who uses terror for political ends
items.example: The terrorist was caught at the border.
items.exampleCN: 恐怖分子在边境被抓获。

items.meaning: the practice of using terror as a method
items.example: Terrorism has no single definition in law.
items.exampleCN: 恐怖主义在法律上没有统一定义。

items.example: Armed men terrorized the village.
The agency leads counterterrorism work.
a counterterrorist unit
the terror-filled months of the siege
items.exampleCN: 被围困中充满恐怖的几个月

items.example: Historians still debate state terror under the regime.
items.exampleCN: 史学家仍在讨论该政权治下的国家恐怖。

items.meaning: a web of linked terror groups
items.example: Police mapped the terror network across three cities.
items.exampleCN: 警方绘制出横跨三城的恐怖网络。

latinEntries.meaning: fright, dread; also the frightener in religious texts
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恐惧；宗教文本中的可怖者

definition_zh: 测试；检验；试验；化验；考查；测验
definition_en: to try something to see whether it works or is true, or an examination and similar trial used to measure quality or knowledge
core_image: 把东西放进火里、放进仪器里，看它到底行不行
scene: 实验台上摆着新电池和一盏小灯。The engineer used the lamp to test the battery.
sceneCN: 这里 test 是「检验、测试」（第 1 个义项：试验某物以看其性能）；句意：工程师用小灯来测这块电池。

derivatives.zh: 测试员；测试器（test 加表人或表物后缀构成）
测试；检测（动名词，指测试这件事）
易怒的（与 test 无词源关系，仅形近；源自法语 teste「头」）
证明；圣约（源自拉丁 testari「作证」，与 test 同出「见证」意象）

senses.title: Try something to see if it works
senses.definition: to try or examine something in order to discover whether it works or has the wanted quality
senses.definitionCN: 试用或检查某物，以发现其是否有效或具备想要的品质
senses.example: Engineers test every bridge model before building it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在建桥之前会测试每一个桥梁模型。
senses.why: The core image is the trial: something is put under stress so that its hidden quality shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「试炼」：把东西置于压力之下，让隐藏的品质显形。

senses.title: Check a person's knowledge or skill
senses.definition: to give someone questions or tasks in order to measure their knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 给某人出题或任务以衡量其知识或能力
senses.example: The final test covers all five units of the book.
senses.exampleCN: 期末测验涵盖本书全部五个单元。
senses.why: A trial applied to a person becomes an exam: stress is questions instead of weights.
senses.whyCN: 施加于人的「试炼」就成了考试：压力从重物换成了题目。

senses.title: Medically examine a sample
senses.definition: to examine a sample of blood, urine or other material for signs of illness or substances
senses.definitionCN: 检查血液、尿液等样本以发现疾病或物质
senses.example: Nurses will test the blood sample this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 护士今天下午会化验这份血样。
senses.why: Examination under controlled conditions is still a trial, only run in a laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 在受控条件下检查仍是「试炼」，只是搬进了实验室。

senses.title: An examination as an event
senses.definition: a written or spoken examination of knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或能力的笔试或口试
senses.example: She stayed up all night before the driving test.
senses.exampleCN: 驾照考试前她熬了通宵。
senses.why: The act of testing becomes the name of the event in which the act happens.
senses.whyCN: 测试行为转而命名其发生的那场事件。

senses.title: A trial that reveals true quality
senses.definition: a difficult situation that shows what someone or something is really like
senses.definitionCN: 显示出人或物真实品质的困难处境
senses.example: The long delay put everyone's patience to the test.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的延误考验了每个人的耐心。
senses.why: Difficulty works like the laboratory stress: it separates real quality from claimed quality.
senses.whyCN: 困难起到实验室压力的作用：把真实品质与宣称的品质分开。

intro.en: Test comes from Latin testum, an earthen pot used by alchemists to heat metals. Trying metal in the pot became trying anything, and the word drifted through Old French into English.
intro.cn: test 源自拉丁语 testum——炼金术士焙烧金属用的陶罐。在罐中试炼金属演变为试炼一切，这个词经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Testum meant an earthen vessel, especially the cupel in which gold and silver were refined by fire.
items.cn: testum 意为陶器，尤指用火提炼金银的灰皿。

items.en: Assaying metal in the pot gave the metaphor: purity is what survives the fire.
items.cn: 在罐中检验金属形成了隐喻：纯度就是经火之后剩下的东西。

items.en: Old French test kept both the vessel and the trial of metal, and added the sense of proving a claim.
items.cn: 古法语 test 同时保留器皿与试金之义，并加上「证明主张」的义项。

items.en: English took test in the 14th century as a vessel for refining metal, used by alchemists.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 test，指炼金术士提炼金属的容器。

items.en: By the 16th to 17th century the metaphor had won: tests of loyalty, of courage, and finally school tests.
items.cn: 至十六七世纪，隐喻占了上风：忠诚的考验、勇气的考验，最终是学校的考试。

note.en: The first group shows words that only look like test; the second ranks the words English uses for measuring trials.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词；第二组排列英语中各种「测验类」词。

entries.definition: irritable and quick-tempered; the spelling is a coincidence, from a French word for head
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的；拼写巧合，源自法语「头」一词，与 test 无关

entries.definition: proof or evidence; from Latin testari to witness, sharing the idea of proving, not the pot
entries.definitionCN: 证明；圣约；源自拉丁 testari「作证」，共享「证明」意象而非陶罐

entries.definition: to give evidence in court; from the same Latin proving family as testament
entries.definitionCN: 作证；与 testament 同出拉丁「见证」词族

entries.definition: a formal test, often longer and more official; exam is the short form
entries.definitionCN: 正式考试；常更长更正式，exam 为缩略

entries.definition: a short informal test, often for fun or quick checking
entries.definitionCN: 简短随意的测验，常用于娱乐或快查

entries.definition: a test in real conditions, often of endurance rather than knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 现实条件下的试用，常考验耐力而非知识

normalIntro.en: Real links: the alchemist's pot, the gold that survives fire, the blood test, and the driving test.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：炼金术士的陶罐、经火犹存的真金、血液化验、驾照考试。

normal.en: Test began as a pot in which metal was tried by fire.
normal.cn: test 最初是火中试金的容器。

normal.en: Only pure gold survives the fire, so test means finding what is real.
normal.cn: 只有真金经得住火，所以 test 就是找出真货。

normal.en: A blood test is the old pot in modern glass tubes.
normal.cn: 血液化验就是装进现代玻璃管的旧陶罐。

normal.en: Test the water first: dip a toe before diving in.
normal.cn: test the water：下水前先用脚尖试水。

normal.en: Put your patience to the test: the fire now burns your temper.
normal.cn: 「put one's patience to the test」：这一回火烧的是你的脾气。

abstract.en: Every test is a small fire that burns away the claims and leaves the facts.
abstract.cn: 每场测试都是一小簇火，烧掉宣称，留下事实。

abstract.en: Pressure does not create quality; it reveals it.
abstract.cn: 压力不创造品质，它只是显影品质。

abstract.en: A question is a weight placed on the mind to see if it holds.
abstract.cn: 问题就是压在头脑上的重物，看它撑不撑得住。

examples.en: The lab will test the water samples for lead.
examples.cn: 实验室将检测水样中的铅。

examples.en: He passed his driving test on the first attempt.
examples.cn: 他一次就通过了驾照考试。

examples.en: Months of delays tested the team's patience.
examples.cn: 数月的拖延考验着团队的耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴死它」——考试时把答案死死贴在桌上也考不过，还得老老实实测 → test 测试、考验

root: 拉丁语 testum「陶罐、试金灰皿」→ 古法语 test → 英语；由「火中试金」引申出一切测试、考试与考验。

sensesIntro.en: From the alchemist's pot, test grew into trying things, examining people, checking samples, naming the exam itself, and finally any hardship that reveals true quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 从炼金陶罐出发，test 长出试物、考人、验样本、命名考试，最终指一切显露真实品质的艰难处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: metal tried in fire, purity revealed by what survives.
core.cn: 核心意象：火中试金，靠剩下来的东西显出纯度。

branches.en: Trying an object under stress is the oldest branch.
branches.cn: 对物件施压试验是最老的一支。

branches.en: The same trial pointed at a person becomes an exam.
branches.cn: 同一试炼指向人便成了考试。

branches.en: Laboratory checks and exam events carry the pot into modern life.
branches.cn: 化验与考试把陶罐带进现代生活。

branches.en: Hardship is the fire; character is the gold.
branches.cn: 困难是火，品格是真金。

branches.en: What survives the trial is the only honest answer.
branches.cn: 经试炼而存者，才是唯一诚实的答案。

intro.en: Test is short and mostly stands alone; the family adds -er, -ing, and the separate Latin witness family of testify and testament.
intro.cn: test 本身短小、多独立使用；词族加上 -er、-ing，另有源自拉丁「见证」的 testify 与 testament 一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin testum is the pot; a different Latin root, testis meaning witness, gives testify, testament and attestation. The two families share spelling, not origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testum 是陶罐；另一个拉丁词根 testis「见证人」给出 testify、testament 与 attestation。两族拼写相近，来源不同。

items.meaning: a person or device that tests
items.example: A breath tester checks the driver.

items.meaning: the act or process of testing
items.example: Testing of the vaccine took two years.

items.meaning: to give evidence as a witness
items.example: She testified in court for three hours.
His testimony freed the innocent man.
items.exampleCN: 他的证词洗清了无辜者的罪名。

items.meaning: proof; also a will; the Bible's two covenants
items.example: The ruins are a testament to the old city's wealth.
items.exampleCN: 遗迹是古城富庶的证明。

items.meaning: to confirm that something is true
items.example: Experts attested the painting's age.
items.exampleCN: 专家证实了这幅画的年代。

items.example: Students protested the fee rise.

items.meaning: a glass tube for laboratory tests
items.example: The baby was conceived in a test tube.
items.exampleCN: 这个婴儿是试管受孕的。

items.meaning: a case tried to set a legal precedent
items.example: The court chose it as a test case.

latinEntries.meaning: earthen vessel; cupel for refining metal
to bear witness, to make a will

definition_zh: 文本；正文；课文；文字材料；发短信
definition_en: the written words of a book or document as opposed to pictures or notes, or to send someone a written message on a phone
core_image: 一张纸上一行行真正的字：不是边角的批注，而是正文本身
scene: 课堂上老师让大家先看图再看字。Read the text on page ten before answering the questions.
sceneCN: 这里 text 是「课文；正文」（第 1 个义项：书页上与图片、注释相对的正文文字）；句意：答题前先读第十页的课文。

derivatives.zh: 文本的；正文的（text 加形容词后缀 -ual 构成）
质地；纹理（同出拉丁 texere「编织」，指织出来的手感）
上下文；语境（con- 加 texere 词根，指与正文织在一起的周边文字）
教科书（text 与 book 复合）

senses.title: The main written words
senses.definition: the actual words of a book, article or document, as opposed to pictures, tables or notes
senses.definitionCN: 书、文章或文件的正文文字，与图片、表格或注释相对
senses.example: Look at the picture first, then read the text beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 先看图，再读旁边的正文。
senses.why: The word separates what is woven from what is added: the main cloth of words against the trimmings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「织出来的」与「附加的」分开：正文的字布相对于边角装饰。

senses.title: A written work studied as literature
senses.definition: a written work treated as an object of study, especially in literary or religious criticism
senses.definitionCN: 被当作研究对象的书，尤用于文学或宗教批评
senses.example: Students compare two ancient texts of the same poem.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们比较同一首诗的两个古文本。
senses.why: Once words are fixed in writing, the fixed thing itself can be handled, compared and argued over as a text.
senses.whyCN: 文字一经写定，写定的东西本身就可被当作文本摆弄、比较、争论。

senses.title: A message on a phone
senses.definition: a written message sent by mobile phone
senses.definitionCN: 用手机发送的书面讯息
senses.example: I got a text from her an hour ago.
senses.exampleCN: 一小时前我收到了她的短信。
senses.why: The smallest modern text: written words stripped down to fit a screen and a thumb.
senses.whyCN: 最小的现代「文本」：被屏幕和拇指削到极简的书面语。

senses.title: To send a text message
senses.definition: to send someone a written message using a mobile phone
senses.definitionCN: 用手机给某人发书面讯息
senses.example: Text me when you arrive at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 到车站后给我发短信。
senses.why: The noun moves into verb position the way English loves: the message names the act of sending it.
senses.whyCN: 名词顺势转成动词：讯息之名加给了发送的动作。

senses.title: A passage quoted or used as basis
senses.definition: a short passage from a book, especially one chosen as the subject of a talk or sermon
senses.definitionCN: 书中的短段文字，尤指被选作演讲或布道主题者
senses.example: The priest chose a text from John's gospel for the sermon.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师从约翰福音里选了段经文作讲道底本。
senses.why: A chosen passage stands alone as the base the speaker weaves the talk around.
senses.whyCN: 被选出的段落独立出来，成为讲话者围绕编织的底本。

intro.en: Text is woven: Latin texere meant to weave, and textus was the fabric of a discourse, the thing woven out of words. The weaving image survives in texture and context too.
intro.cn: text 是「织」出来的：拉丁语 texere 意为编织，textus 是话语织成的布料。织的意象同样活在 texture 与 context 里。

items.en: Texere meant to weave, and textus named the woven thing, later the tissue of a written argument.
items.cn: texere 意为编织，textus 指织成之物，后指写成的论证之「织体」。

items.en: The same root gives texture, the feel of weave, and context, the words woven together with a passage.
items.cn: 同一词根给出 texture（织物的手感）与 context（与段落织在一起的前后文字）。

items.en: Old French texte carried the Latin word in the sense of the authoritative wording of scripture.
items.cn: 古法语 texte 承接拉丁词，指圣经经文的权威字句。

items.en: English took text in the 14th century, first for the scriptural passage behind a sermon, then for any body of writing.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪借入 text，先指布道所依的经文段，后泛指一切书面文字。

items.en: Printing, criticism and finally the mobile phone extended the word to any written matter and to texting.
items.cn: 印刷、文学批评，最后是手机，把这个词扩展到一切书面材料与「发短信」。

note.en: The first group collects the weaving family that text belongs to; the second separates text from neighbouring writing words.
note.cn: 第一组收拢 text 所属的「编织」词族；第二组把 text 与相邻的书写类词分开。

entries.definition: the feel and pattern of a surface, from Latin texere to weave; same weaving root, different sense path
entries.definitionCN: 质地；纹理；同出 texere「编织」词根但义路不同

entries.definition: the words woven around a passage; con- means together and the rest is the weaving root
entries.definitionCN: 上下文；语境；con- 表「共同」，词干即「织」

entries.definition: a false reason woven in front of an action; pre- means before
entries.definitionCN: 借口；托辞；pre- 表「在前」，把假理由「织」在行动之前

entries.definition: a section of writing; shorter than a text and without the idea of the whole work
entries.definitionCN: 段落；指作品中的一部分，不指整部著作

entries.definition: sacred writing; text once meant almost exactly this in English
entries.definitionCN: 经文；text 早期的含义几乎就是它

entries.definition: the exact choice of words; narrower than text, which names the whole written body
entries.definitionCN: 措辞；比 text 窄，text 指整篇书面文字

normalIntro.en: Real links: the weaving root texere, the family of texture and context, the sermon text, and the modern text message.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：编织词根 texere、texture 与 context 词族、布道经文、以及现代短信。

normal.en: Text comes from weaving: words woven line by line like thread.
normal.cn: text 来自编织：文字像线一样一行行织出。

normal.en: Texture is what weaving feels like; context is what is woven with it.
normal.cn: texture 是织物的手感；context 是与它织在一起的东西。

normal.en: A preacher once spoke from a chosen text; now a teenager speaks by texting.
normal.cn: 牧师曾依选定的经文讲道；如今少年靠发短信说话。

normal.en: Pretext: a reason woven in front to cover the real one.
normal.cn: pretext：织在前面的理由，盖住真理由。

normal.en: Textbook: the book that holds the set texts for study.
normal.cn: textbook：装着指定课文的教材。

abstract.en: Every text is cloth: threads of words, woven tight enough to carry meaning.
abstract.cn: 每篇文本都是布：文字作线，织得够紧才承得住意义。

abstract.en: Cut a sentence from its context and the weave frays.
abstract.cn: 把句子从语境中剪出来，布就散线。

abstract.en: A text message is a woven ribbon only ten centimetres long.
abstract.cn: 短信只是一条十厘米长的织带。

examples.en: The printed text differs slightly from the manuscript.
examples.cn: 印本正文与手稿略有出入。

examples.en: She texted her mother as soon as the plane landed.
examples.cn: 飞机一落地她就给妈妈发了短信。

examples.en: Scholars still argue about the original text of the play.
examples.cn: 学者们仍在争论这部剧本的原文。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴克斯特」——把课文一段段贴在课桌上克敌制胜，先贴先读 → text 文本、课文

root: 拉丁语 texere「编织」→ textus「织成之物、话语织体」→ 古法语 texte → 英语；同根词 texture、context、pretext。

sensesIntro.en: Text starts as the woven body of words against its trimmings, becomes an object of study, shrinks into a phone message, turns into a verb, and can still name the single passage a sermon is built on.
sensesIntro.cn: text 从与装饰相对的「文字织体」出发，成为研究对象，缩成手机短信，转为动词，也仍可指布道所依的单一经段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words woven line by line into cloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：文字如线，一行行织成布。

branches.en: The main cloth of words against pictures and notes.
branches.cn: 相对于图片与注释的文字主布。

branches.en: The fixed cloth becomes an object to study and compare.
branches.cn: 写定的织体成为可研究比较的对象。

branches.en: The message shrinks the cloth to a ribbon, then names the sending.
branches.cn: 短信把布缩成细带，进而命名发送动作。

branches.en: One thread cut out becomes the base of a sermon.
branches.cn: 剪出的一根线成为布道的底本。

branches.en: Weaving and studying share the same cloth.
branches.cn: 编织与研究共享同一块布。

intro.en: The weaving root texere/tec- builds a wide family: text, texture, context, pretext, textile, and even technology through Greek craft-words.
intro.cn: 编织词根 texere/tec- 构建了庞大词族：text、texture、context、pretext、textile，甚至经希腊工匠词进入 technology。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere and textus sit under the whole family; the root also gave textor, a weaver, and textura, the structure of weaving.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族建立在拉丁 texere 与 textus 之上；词根还给出 textor「织工」与 textura「织构」。

items.example: A textual error crept into the reprint.
items.exampleCN: 重印本混入了一处文字错误。

items.meaning: the words woven around a passage
items.example: Guess the meaning from context.
He left early on the pretext of illness.

items.meaning: the feel or structure of a surface
items.example: The fabric has a rough texture.

items.meaning: a woven fabric; relating to weaving
items.example: The city is a textile centre.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市是纺织业中心。

items.example: Buy the textbook before class.

items.meaning: the meaning woven beneath the words
items.example: The subtext of the letter was anger.
items.exampleCN: 这封信的潜台词是愤怒。

items.example: He texted twice last night.

items.meaning: the habit of sending phone messages
items.example: Texting while driving is dangerous.

latinEntries.meaning: a woven thing; the tissue of a discourse

definition_zh: 纺织品；织物；纺织原料；纺织的
definition_en: cloth made by weaving or knitting, or the material from which such cloth is made
core_image: 无数细线在织机上纵横交错，最后压成一整匹平整的布
scene: 工厂把成卷的棉纱送进织机，出来时已是一整匹布。The mill fed rolls of cotton yarn into the loom, and a bolt of textile came out.
sceneCN: 这里指「织成的布匹」（第 1 个义项：纺织成品）；句意为工厂把成卷的棉纱送进织机，出来时已是一整匹纺织品。可辨识物件：棉纱卷、织机、布匹、传送带。

derivatives.zh: 纺织产品；纺织业（由基础词加表示复数的后缀构成，语义偏移为商品类别与行业）
纺织品设计师（由基础词与表示「设计师」的词复合，语义收窄为职业）
以纺织材料为基础的（由基础词与表示「以……为基础」的词复合，语义偏移为材料属性）
类似纺织品的（由基础词加表示「像……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）

senses.title: Woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth produced by weaving, knitting or another fabric-making process
senses.definitionCN: 通过机织、针织或其他制布工艺生产出来的布
senses.example: A bolt of textile came out of the loom.
senses.exampleCN: 一整匹布从织机里出来。
senses.why: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to weave'. A textile is literally a woven thing, so the sense begins with the finished cloth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个意为「编织」的拉丁动词。纺织品字面上就是「被织成的东西」，因此词义从成品布开始。

senses.title: The textile industry
senses.definition: the industry that makes cloth, usually referred to in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 制造布料的工业，通常用复数形式指整个行业
senses.example: The town's textiles employed half its workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇的纺织业雇用了半数工人。
senses.why: An industry named after its product uses the plural to mean the sector as a whole, not a pile of individual cloths.
senses.whyCN: 以产品命名的行业用复数指整个部门，而不是指一堆具体的布。

senses.title: Fibre material for cloth
senses.definition: the fibre, yarn or filament from which cloth is made
senses.definitionCN: 用来制作布料的纤维、纱线或长丝
senses.example: The lab tests textile before it reaches the loom.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在原料上织机之前先做检测。
senses.why: Because the finished cloth and its material are stages of one process, the same noun serves for both, distinguished by context.
senses.whyCN: 成品布与原料是同一过程的不同阶段，因此同一个名词兼指两者，靠语境区分。

senses.title: Relating to cloth
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：与织物有关的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of cloth, weaving or the cloth trade'
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示「织物的、织造的或纺织业的」
senses.example: Textile exports rose for the third year.
senses.exampleCN: 纺织品出口连续第三年增长。
senses.why: As an adjective the word simply labels a field, so textile exports or textile design means the cloth sector rather than a particular cloth.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是给一个领域贴标签，因此纺织品出口或纺织品设计指的是布料行业，而非某一块布。

senses.title: Industrial and technical fabrics
senses.definition: engineered fabrics made for strength, filtration, protection or other technical uses
senses.definitionCN: 为强度、过滤、防护等技术用途而设计的织物
senses.example: The car uses technical textile in its seats.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的座椅用了技术纺织品。
senses.why: Modern fibres can be designed for a job rather than for appearance, so the word now covers fabrics that never reach a wardrobe.
senses.whyCN: 现代纤维可以为功能而非外观来设计，因此这个词现在也涵盖根本不会进入衣柜的织物。

senses.title: Non-woven fabric
senses.definition: fabric made by bonding or felting fibres rather than by weaving them
senses.definitionCN: 通过黏合或毡合纤维、而非编织制成的布
senses.example: The mask is made of non-woven textile.
senses.exampleCN: 这只口罩由非织造布制成。
senses.why: The category expanded past its own etymology: cloth can now be made without a loom, yet it still belongs to the textile family.
senses.whyCN: 这个类别超出了自身的词源：如今不用织机也能制布，但它仍属于纺织品家族。

senses.title: Textile design as a field
senses.definition: the discipline of designing patterns, structures and surfaces for cloth
senses.definitionCN: 为布料设计图案、结构与表面的学科
senses.example: She studied textile at an art school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在艺术学校学习纺织品设计。
senses.why: Once cloth became a designed surface, the noun named a course of study and a profession, not only a material.
senses.whyCN: 当布料成为被设计的表面，这个名词就指一门课程与一种职业，而不只是材料。

senses.title: Household textile goods
senses.definition: cloth goods sold for the home, such as bedding, towels and curtains, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 面向家庭销售的布制品，如床品、毛巾与窗帘，通常用复数
senses.example: The shop sells home textiles on the ground floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在一层卖家用纺织品。
senses.why: Retail groups cloth by where it is used. The plural marks a product category rather than any single woven piece.
senses.whyCN: 零售业按使用场所给布料分类。复数标记的是一个商品类别，而不是某一件织物。

intro.en: Textile comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'woven', built on the verb texere 'to weave'. The same verb also gives text, texture, context and tissue. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: textile 来自一个意为「织成的」的拉丁形容词，其动词是 texere「编织」。同一个动词还给出 text、texture、context 与 tissue。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin texere meant 'to weave, plait, construct'. A text was first something woven, and only later something written.
items.cn: 拉丁 texere 意为「编织、编结、构造」。最初 text 指织成的东西，后来才指写成的东西。

items.en: The adjective textilis 'woven, able to be woven' produced the noun textilis in later usage, and English took the adjective directly.
items.cn: 形容词 textilis 意为「织成的、可织的」，在后来的用法中产生名词形式；英语直接借入了这个形容词。

items.en: French textile mediated the word in the seventeenth century, when cloth manufacture was becoming an organised trade in Europe.
items.cn: 法语 textile 在十七世纪传递了这个词；当时布料制造在欧洲正变成有组织的行业。

items.en: With mechanised spinning and weaving, textile became the standard word for mill-made cloth and for the industry itself.
items.cn: 随着机械化纺纱与织造，textile 成为工厂制布以及整个行业的标准词。

items.en: Synthetic and non-woven fibres widened the word in the twentieth century, so it now covers fabrics that are not woven at all.
items.cn: 合成纤维与非织造纤维在二十世纪拓宽了这个词，因此它现在也涵盖根本不经编织的布。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of texere before Latin is unsettled, and the Indo-European root often cited for it is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：texere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，常被引用的印欧词根属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same weaving root that now mean different things; group two holds everyday words for cloth.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「编织」词根、但现在意思不同的词；第二组是表示布料的日常词。

entries.definition: relating to a text or wording; it shares the weaving root but followed the written branch.
entries.definitionCN: 与文本或措辞有关的；它共享编织词根，却走了「书写」这一支。

entries.definition: the feel or arrangement of a surface; it keeps the woven image as a quality rather than an object.
entries.definitionCN: 表面的手感或结构；它把编织意象保留为一种性质，而非物件。

entries.definition: written or printed words; historically 'that which is woven', now entirely separated from cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 书写或印刷的文字；历史上意为「织成之物」，如今已与布料完全分开。

entries.definition: the words around a passage, literally 'woven together'; it belongs to the writing branch, not the cloth trade.
entries.definitionCN: 一段文字周围的词语，字面义为「织在一起」；它属于书写分支，而非纺织行业。

entries.definition: cloth or any material made by joining parts; from Latin fabrica 'workshop', it stresses manufacture rather than weaving.
entries.definitionCN: 布料或任何由部件构成的材料；来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」，强调制造而非编织。

entries.definition: the common word for woven material; it is plainer and less industrial than textile.
entries.definitionCN: 指织物的普通词；比 textile 更朴素，也更少工业色彩。

entries.definition: any substance used to make something; it is broader than textile and says nothing about weaving.
entries.definitionCN: 用来制作某物的任何物质；比 textile 宽泛，不涉及编织。

entries.definition: cloth arranged in folds as curtains or hangings; it names a use of fabric rather than the fabric itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以褶皱形式布置成窗帘或悬挂物的布；它指布料的用途，而非布料本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'to weave', so textile is literally 'the woven thing'.
normal.cn: 词根意为「编织」，所以 textile 字面上就是「被织成的东西」。

normal.en: Text, texture and context come from the same verb, which is why a text can be described as woven.
normal.cn: text、texture 与 context 都出自同一个动词，这也是为什么一篇文本可以被形容为「织成」的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the industry: textile industry, textile mill, textile production.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出行业：纺织工业、纺织厂、纺织品生产。

normal.en: The plural textiles names goods and the sector, not several separate cloths.
normal.cn: 复数形式指商品与行业部门，而不是几块分开的布。

normal.en: Technical textile shows that modern fabrics may be engineered rather than woven.
normal.cn: 技术纺织品说明现代织物可以是设计出来的，而不一定是织出来的。

abstract.en: Picture thousands of threads that only become a surface when they cross.
abstract.cn: 想象成千上万根线，只有交错之后才成为一片表面。

abstract.en: Picture a word and a cloth made by the same gesture of binding strands.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词与一块布，由同一个「把线束在一起」的动作做成。

abstract.en: Picture a material that can be flat, stiff, soft or filtering without changing its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一种材料，可以是平的、硬的、软的或用于过滤，却不必改名。

examples.en: The museum displays textile from the eighteenth-century mill.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出十八世纪工厂生产的纺织品。

examples.en: Textile workers demanded cleaner air in the spinning rooms.
examples.cn: 纺织工人要求在纺纱车间里呼吸更干净的空气。

examples.en: The designers mixed textile with recycled plastic.
examples.cn: 设计师把织物与再生塑料混用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特克斯太尔」—— 把特别细密的线一根根织成整匹布 → 纺织品

root: 拉丁 textilis「织成的」，来自 texere「编织、编结」；同一动词还派生 text、texture、context、tissue。texere 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，常见印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: fibres are woven into cloth, cloth becomes an industry, a material, a field of design and a retail category, and finally a family of engineered fabrics that need no loom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一过程展开：纤维被织成布，布再成为行业、材料、设计领域与零售类别，最后成为一个无需织机的工程织物家族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thousands of threads crossing on a loom until they hold together as one surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：成千上万根线在织机上交错，直到合成一整片表面。

branches.en: FROM FIBRE TO CLOTH: the material and the finished cloth are two ends of one process.
branches.cn: 从纤维到布：原料与成品布是同一过程的两端。

branches.en: GOODS AND SECTOR: the plural covers both mill products and the trade that makes them.
branches.cn: 商品与行业：复数形式既涵盖工厂产品，也涵盖制造它们的行业。

branches.en: AS A LABEL: the adjective marks anything belonging to cloth or the cloth trade.
branches.cn: 作为标签：形容词标记任何属于布料或纺织业的事物。

branches.en: BEYOND WEAVING: technical and non-woven fabrics keep the family name after leaving the loom.
branches.cn: 超越编织：技术织物与非织造布在离开织机后仍保留这个家族名称。

branches.en: AS DISCIPLINE: design turns cloth into a subject with patterns, structures and training.
branches.cn: 作为学科：设计把布料变成一门有图案、结构与训练体系的科目。

intro.en: Textile is one branch of a large Latin family built on weaving. The same root reaches writing, surface feel and the surrounding words of a passage.
intro.cn: textile 是以「编织」为核心的一大型拉丁词族中的一支。同一词根还通到书写、表面手感以及一段文字周围的词语。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere gives textile, text, texture, context and tissue; the past participle textus is literally 'a woven thing'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 texere 给出 textile、text、texture、context 与 tissue；过去分词 textus 字面义就是「织成之物」。

items.structure: texere, texui, textum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb covers both cloth and language.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词既覆盖布料，也覆盖语言。

items.example: The root appears in both fabric and writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时出现在织物与书写中。

items.example: The adjective became the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词变成了英语名词。

items.example: Textile fills the mill's output.
items.exampleCN: 纺织品构成工厂的产出。

items.meaning: the feel or arrangement of a surface
items.example: The texture of the cloth is coarse.
The text runs to forty pages.

items.meaning: the words woven around a passage
items.meaningCN: 环绕一段文字的上下文
items.example: Read the sentence in context.
items.exampleCN: 把这个句子放在上下文中读。

items.example: The word first meant a ribbon of cloth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初指一条布带。

items.example: Textiles dominate the region's exports.
items.exampleCN: 纺织品占该地区出口的主要部分。

items.meaning: a person who designs cloth patterns
items.example: The textile designer works with jacquard looms.
items.exampleCN: 这位纺织品设计师使用提花织机工作。

items.example: The wall has a textile-like finish.
items.exampleCN: 这面墙有类似织物的饰面。

definition_zh: 比（用于比较）；（除……）之外；超出
definition_en: a word used after a comparative to introduce the second part of a comparison, or after words such as rather and other
core_image: 天平两端：一边压下去，另一边被 than 抬到秤上作对照
scene: 两个孩子站在身高尺前比个子。Tom is taller than his elder sister now.
sceneCN: 这里 than 是比较连词「比」（第 1 个义项：引出比较对象）；句意：汤姆现在比他姐姐还高了。

pos.zh: 比；用于引出比较的第二方

derivatives.zh: 然后；当时（与 than 同出古英语同一副词，后拼写分化）
除……之外（固定短语，than 保留其「除外」用法）
而不是（固定短语，表选择弃取）

senses.title: Introduce the second part of a comparison
senses.definition: used after a comparative adjective or adverb to link the two things being compared
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较级形容词或副词之后，连接被比较的两方
senses.example: My new phone is cheaper than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 我的新手机比旧的便宜。
senses.why: Comparison needs a scale and a second pan; than is the hook that hangs the second pan on the balance.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要标尺与另一个秤盘；than 就是把第二个秤盘挂上天平的钩子。

senses.title: After rather and other: besides or instead of
senses.definition: used after rather, other, else to mean besides, instead of, or except
senses.definitionCN: 用于 rather、other、else 之后，表示除……之外、而非
senses.example: There was no one in the room other than the guard.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里除了保安没有别人。
senses.why: The comparing pan is emptied of all but one item, so than now marks what is set aside.
senses.whyCN: 比较的秤盘被清空到只剩一件，于是 than 标出被搁在一旁的那个东西。

senses.title: Expressing exceeding a quantity
senses.definition: used after more, less, fewer to show a quantity above or below a number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于 more、less、fewer 之后，表示超出或不足某个数量
senses.example: More than two hundred students joined the club.
senses.exampleCN: 两百多名学生加入了社团。
senses.why: When one pan holds a number, than measures the overflow beyond it.
senses.whyCN: 当秤盘上放的是数字，than 就量出溢出秤盘的那部分。

intro.en: Than and then were once the same Old English word. The adverb of time drifted into comparison, and in early Modern English the spellings split: than for comparing, then for time.
intro.cn: than 与 then 原是同一个古英语词。时间副词漂移出比较用法，近代英语早期拼写分化：than 管比较，then 管时间。

items.en: The adverb þanne and þonne meant then, at that time, and also served as a comparison particle.
items.cn: 古英语副词 þanne/þonne 意为「那时、然后」，也用作比较小品词。

items.en: The word goes back to a Germanic demonstrative adverb related to the word for that, pointing at one side of a comparison.
items.cn: 它可追溯到日耳曼语的指示副词，与「那个」一词相关，指向比较中的一端。

items.en: Middle English wrote thanne, thenne, pan and ban; the senses of time and comparison still overlapped freely.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 thanne、thenne、pan、ban；时间义与比较义仍自由交叠。

items.en: In comparative sentences the word kept the correlative pattern: so much, than so much, the pointer swinging between the pans.
items.cn: 在比较句中它保持呼应格局：这么多，than 又那么多，指针在两盘之间摆动。

items.en: By the seventeenth century usage fixed than for comparison and then for time, though confusion continued in speech.
items.cn: 至十七世纪，用法固定为 than 管比较、then 管时间，尽管口语中仍有混用。

note.en: The first group shows the word than split from and collides with; the second gathers comparison words that share its job.
note.cn: 第一组展示与 than 同源分化及相撞的词；第二组收拢承担比较功能的词。

entries.definition: at that time; once the same Old English word as than, now kept for time
entries.definitionCN: 然后；当时；与 than 同出古英语一词，如今专管时间

entries.definition: the demonstrative pronoun whose Old English form gave the adverb family its pointing power
entries.definitionCN: 指示词 that；其古英语形式给了这一副词家族的指向力

entries.definition: only shares the th- spelling family; grammatical relation is different
entries.definitionCN: they；只同属 th- 拼写家族，语法关系不同

entries.definition: introduces equal comparison, where than introduces unequal comparison
entries.definitionCN: 引出同等比较；than 引出不等比较

entries.definition: an explicit comparison phrase, heavier and more formal than than
entries.definitionCN: 显性比较短语，比 than 更重更正式

entries.definition: marks contrast without a scale, where than always stands on a scale
entries.definitionCN: 标示无标尺的对比；than 总是站在标尺上

normalIntro.en: Real links: the shared Old English word with then, the demonstrative that behind it, and the fixed pairs rather than and other than.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：与 then 同一古英语词、其背后的指示词 that、以及 rather than 与 other than 固定搭配。

normal.en: Than and then were one word; spelling split them in the 1600s.
normal.cn: than 与 then 曾是一个词，十七世纪拼写才分家。

normal.en: Than hangs the second pan on the comparison scale.
normal.cn: than 把第二个秤盘挂上比较天平。

normal.en: Rather than picks one and drops the other.
normal.cn: rather than 选一个、弃另一个。

normal.en: Other than means every pan is empty except that one.
normal.cn: other than 表示除那一盘外全都倒空。

normal.en: More than a number counts the overflow.
normal.cn: more than 加数字量出超出之量。

abstract.en: Comparison is invisible until a word like than builds the bridge between two pans.
abstract.cn: 没有 than 这类词架桥，比较就只是两个看不见的秤盘。

abstract.en: Every than hides a smaller and a bigger, waiting for the sentence to say which.
abstract.cn: 每个 than 都藏着大与小，等句子来宣布谁是谁。

abstract.en: Time and comparison share one ancestor: pointing is pointing, whether at a moment or at a measure.
abstract.cn: 时间与比较同宗：指向就是指向，无论指向时刻还是指向量度。

examples.en: She runs faster than anyone else in the team.
examples.cn: 她跑得比队里其他任何人都快。

examples.en: I would rather walk than wait for the bus.
examples.cn: 我宁愿走路也不想等公交。

examples.en: More than half the class passed the exam.
examples.cn: 全班超过一半的人通过了考试。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「掸」——天平一高一低，用手掸一下另一盘就比出来了 → than 比

root: 古英语副词 þanne/þonne（「那时」，兼作比较小品词）→ 日耳曼指示副词，与「那个」同源；近代英语与 then 拼写分化。

sensesIntro.en: Than begins as a pointing adverb pressed into comparison service, then extends to exceptive rather/other than and to quantities that overflow a number.
sensesIntro.cn: than 起于被征来作比较的指向副词，延伸到除外的 rather/other than，再延伸到超出数字的量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pan hung on the balance of comparison.
core.cn: 核心意象：把第二个秤盘挂上比较的天平。

branches.en: The second pan of every comparative sentence.
branches.cn: 每个比较句的第二个秤盘。

branches.en: The pan emptied until one item is left aside.
branches.cn: 秤盘被倒空，只余被搁置的一项。

branches.en: The pan that measures how far a number is exceeded.
branches.cn: 量出数字被超出多远的秤盘。

branches.en: Unequal comparison and overflow share one hook.
branches.cn: 不等比较与超出共用同一个钩子。

branches.en: Exceptive than keeps only the pointing, drops the scale.
branches.cn: 除外的 than 只留指向，丢掉标尺。

intro.en: Than has no affixes of its own; its story is told by the family of pointing words it split from.
intro.cn: than 自身无词缀；它的故事由它所从中分化的指向词家族讲述。

latinIntro.en: Than is Germanic, not Latin; the Latin comparison words listed here are given only as contrast.
latinIntro.cn: than 属日耳曼语源而非拉丁；此处拉丁比较词仅作对照。

items.example: þanne gave both then and than.
items.exampleCN: þanne 同时生出了 then 与 than。

items.example: Then the door opened.

items.meaning: the pointing word behind the adverb family
items.meaningCN: 指示词，比 than 更古老
items.example: That book is mine.
Walk rather than drive.
No one other than Tom came.
More than ten guests came.
She works harder than ever.
items.exampleCN: 她比以往任何时候都更用功。

items.meaningCN: 要求 than 出现的比较级框架
items.example: Bigger than, smaller than, better than.
items.exampleCN: bigger than、smaller than、better than 这类比较结构。

definition_zh: 感谢；谢谢；道谢；责怪（旧用法）
definition_en: to express gratitude to someone for something done or given
core_image: 把心里的感激说出口，像把一件收下的礼物再递回去一件
scene: 老邻居冒雨帮她把快递搬进门。She thanked the neighbour and shut the door against the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 thank 是「感谢」（第 1 个义项：向某人表达感激）；句意：她谢过邻居，关门挡住雨水。

derivatives.zh: 感激的；欣慰的（thank 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成）
感激地；幸而（thankful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成）
感恩；感恩节（thank 与 giving 复合，指把感谢献出）
吃力不讨好的（thank 加 -less，指得不到感谢的）

senses.title: Express gratitude in words
senses.definition: to tell someone that you are grateful for something they have done
senses.definitionCN: 用话语告诉某人你对其所做的事心存感激
senses.example: He thanked the driver as he got off the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 下车时他向司机道了谢。
senses.why: Gratitude felt is gratitude spoken: the verb requires the words to leave the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 心里的感激要变成嘴上的话：这个动词要求感激被说出来。

senses.title: Attribute something good or bad to someone
senses.definition: to hold someone responsible for something, in phrases like have sb to thank for
senses.definitionCN: 把某事的因果归于某人，用于 have sb to thank for 等短语
senses.example: We have the early rain to thank for the good harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 好收成要感谢早来的雨水。
senses.why: Gratitude points at a cause; pointing can praise or blame, so the frame bends both ways.
senses.whyCN: 感激指向原因；指向既能夸也能怪，所以这个框架两个方向都弯得动。

senses.title: Polite refusal or acceptance
senses.definition: used politely to refuse an offer or to acknowledge one, as in No, thank you
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地婉拒或领受他人的好意，如 No, thank you
senses.example: No, thank you, I have had enough tea.
senses.exampleCN: 不用了谢谢，茶我喝够了。
senses.why: Even refusal is wrapped in gratitude, to soften the closing of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 连拒绝也要裹上感激，好让合拢的手显得柔和。

intro.en: Thank is native Germanic, from a root meaning thought: to thank was once to think good of someone. Nouns like thought and thank share the thinking root.
intro.cn: thank 是日耳曼本族词，词根义为「想」：感谢最初就是「心里念着某人的好」。thought 与 thank 共享这个思考词根。

items.en: The reconstructed root thangk- meant to think, to feel a thought about someone.
items.cn: 重构词根 thangk- 意为想、对某人心存念想。

items.en: The noun þanc meant thought, favour, gratitude; the verb þancian meant to think gratefully of someone.
items.cn: 古英语名词 þanc 意为想法、恩惠、感激；动词 þancian 意为感念某人。

items.en: The same root gave the noun þoht, which became modern thought; thinking and thanking are twins.
items.cn: 同一词根给出名词 þoht，即现代 thought；「想」与「谢」是孪生兄弟。

items.en: The verb settled into thanken, used with indirect objects, and the plural thanks appeared as a set phrase.
items.cn: 中古英语动词定型为 thanken，带间接宾语使用；复数 thanks 作为固定语出现。

items.en: Thank you froze into the everyday formula, and thanks to shifted from gratitude to plain causation.
items.cn: thank you 冻结成日常套语；thanks to 则从感激滑向单纯的原因表达。

note.en: The first group follows the thinking root through its twin words; the second compares the everyday gratitude words.
note.cn: 第一组沿「思考」词根走完孪生词；第二组比较日常感谢语。

entries.definition: an idea; from the same Old English root as thank, the thinking ancestor
entries.definitionCN: 想法；与 thank 同出古英语词根，「思考」是祖先

entries.definition: glad and grateful; the adjective of the thank family
entries.definitionCN: 感激的；欣慰的；thank 词族的形容词

entries.definition: getting no gratitude in return, like a thankless job
entries.definitionCN: 得不到感谢的，如吃力不讨好的差事

entries.definition: to value and be grateful for something, often more formal than thank
entries.definitionCN: 珍视并感激；常比 thank 正式

entries.definition: the feeling itself, where thank is the act of expressing it
entries.definitionCN: 感激之情本身；thank 是表达感激的动作

entries.definition: to show that you have received something, without the warmth of thanks
entries.definitionCN: 确认收到；不带 thank 的暖意

normalIntro.en: Real links: the think-thank root pair, thankful and thankless, Thanksgiving the holiday, and the formula thank you.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：think-thank 词根对、thankful 与 thankless、感恩节 Thanksgiving、以及套语 thank you。

normal.en: Thank and thought share one root: to thank is to think well of someone.
normal.cn: thank 与 thought 同根：感谢就是心里念着某人的好。

normal.en: Thankful is full of thanks; thankless is empty of them.
normal.cn: thankful 是装满感谢的；thankless 是空空的。

normal.en: Thanksgiving gives thanks, literally the act of thanks-giving.
normal.cn: Thanksgiving 字面上就是「献出感谢」的动作。

normal.en: No, thank you: even refusal wears a grateful face.
normal.cn: No, thank you：连拒绝也戴着感激的脸。

normal.en: Thanks to the rain, or thanks to the delay, both are pointing at a cause.
normal.cn: thanks to the rain 或 thanks to the delay，都是在指向原因。

abstract.en: Gratitude is thought turning around to face its giver.
abstract.cn: 感激是念头转回身，面对它的给予者。

abstract.en: A thankless task keeps giving while nothing comes back.
abstract.cn: 吃力不讨好的差事只出不进。

abstract.en: Every thank you is a small debt settled with words instead of money.
abstract.cn: 每句谢谢都是用话语而非金钱结清的小债。

examples.en: I thanked her for staying late to help.
examples.cn: 我感谢她留下来帮忙到很晚。

examples.en: Thank goodness the storm passed before dawn.
examples.cn: 谢天谢地，风暴在天亮前过去了。

examples.en: The volunteers deserve our warmest thanks.
examples.cn: 志愿者们值得我们最诚挚的感谢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三克油」——别人帮你，你说 three grams of oil 都舍得给，可见多感激 → thank 感谢

root: 日耳曼词根 thangk-「想」→ 古英语 þanc「感念」/þancian「感谢」→ 英语；同根词 thought、thankful、thanksgiving。

sensesIntro.en: Thank grows from thinking well of someone into spoken gratitude, then into pointing at causes for praise or blame, and finally into the polite wrapper around refusals.
sensesIntro.cn: thank 从「念人之好」长出说出声的感激，再到指向可褒可贬的原因，最后成为包裹婉拒的礼貌用语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thought of someone's goodness, spoken out loud.
core.cn: 核心意象：对某人好处的念想，被说出了口。

branches.en: The thought leaves the heart and crosses the lips.
branches.cn: 念想离开心底，越过唇边。

branches.en: Pointing at a cause can thank or blame.
branches.cn: 指向原因既可谢亦可怪。

branches.en: Gratitude wraps the closing hand softly.
branches.cn: 感激温柔地裹住合拢的手。

branches.en: Thinking well and counting causes share one gesture.
branches.cn: 念人之好与推究因果共享同一个手势。

branches.en: The formula survives even when the feeling is thin.
branches.cn: 哪怕情意淡薄，套语仍然存活。

intro.en: Thank adds the adjective suffixes -ful and -less, the adverb -ly, and compounds with giving and worth.
intro.cn: thank 加上形容词后缀 -ful 与 -less、副词 -ly，并与 giving、worth 复合。

latinIntro.en: Thank is Germanic, not Latin; the Latin gratitude words listed here serve only as contrast.
latinIntro.cn: thank 属日耳曼语源而非拉丁；所列拉丁感谢词仅作对照。

items.example: We were thankful to reach shore.
Thankfully, no one was hurt.
Looking after the sick is a thankless job.
items.exampleCN: 照料病人是份吃力不讨好的工作。

items.meaning: the act of giving thanks; the November holiday
items.example: They gathered for Thanksgiving dinner.
items.exampleCN: 他们聚在一起吃感恩节晚餐。

items.example: An older translation called it thankworthy.
Thank you for waiting.

items.meaning: because of, often with a hint of luck
items.example: Thanks to the alarm, we caught the train.
items.exampleCN: 多亏闹钟，我们赶上了火车。

items.example: Old proverbs warn against unthankful children.

definition_zh: 谢谢；多谢；（复数）谢意；感谢之情
definition_en: an expression of gratitude, used as an exclamation or as the plural noun of thanks owed or given
core_image: 一句话的感谢被装进复数：一份份谢意可以攒起来，也可以送出去
scene: 同事把落下的伞递还给他。Thanks, I thought I had lost it for good.
sceneCN: 这里 thanks 是感叹词「谢谢」（第 1 个义项：表达感激的感叹语）；句意：多谢，我还以为再也找不回来了。

derivatives.zh: 感谢（thanks 的动词基形）
感激的（thank 加 -ful 构成）
感恩；感恩节（thanks 感恩的献出）

senses.title: The exclamation of gratitude
senses.definition: a quick spoken expression of gratitude, less formal than thank you
senses.definitionCN: 口头快速表达感激的方式，不如 thank you 正式
senses.example: Thanks for carrying my suitcase upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 多谢你把箱子搬上楼。
senses.why: The plural form alone escaped into speech: many small thanks stacked into one handy word.
senses.whyCN: 只有复数形式逃进了口语：许多小感谢摞成一个顺手的词。

senses.title: The feeling or expression owed
senses.definition: gratitude felt or expressed toward someone, as a plural noun
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有或表达出的感激，作复数名词
senses.example: She sent her thanks to the whole nursing team.
senses.exampleCN: 她向全体护理团队致谢。
senses.why: Thanks become things that can be sent, returned and owed like small coins of goodwill.
senses.whyCN: 谢意成为可以寄出、回赠、亏欠的东西，像善意的小硬币。

senses.title: Because of, in the phrase thanks to
senses.definition: used with to to say that a person or thing caused a result, good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 与 to 连用，表示某人某物导致了结果，好坏皆可
senses.example: Thanks to the fog, the ferry arrived an hour late.
senses.exampleCN: 多亏那场雾，渡轮晚点一小时。
senses.why: The pointed gratitude stretches into plain causation: what you thank becomes simply what happened.
senses.whyCN: 指向性的感激拉长为单纯因果：你感谢的对象干脆变成了事情的原因。

intro.en: Thanks is the Old English noun þanc in its plural, thank passed into the plural and then, as an exclamation, escaped into everyday speech on its own.
intro.cn: thanks 是古英语名词 þanc 的复数形：thank 进入复数后，作为感叹词独自逃进了日常口语。

items.en: The noun þanc meant thought, gratitude and favour, from the Germanic thinking root.
items.cn: 古英语名词 þanc 意为念想、感激、恩惠，出自日耳曼「思考」词根。

items.en: Set phrases like þanc mete, thanks for the meal, already used the plural.
items.cn: 像 þanc mete「谢饭」这样的固定语已经在用复数。

items.en: Middle English kept gramercy and I thank you as polite formulas, with thanks growing behind them.
items.cn: 中古英语把 gramercy 与 I thank you 作为礼貌套语，thanks 在其背后生长。

items.en: By the 16th century thanks alone served as the quick everyday thanks, and many thanks as the fuller one.
items.cn: 至十六世纪，thanks 单独承担快速的日常致谢，many thanks 作更郑重之用。

items.en: The phrase thanks to drifted into causation, able to thank the fog as easily as the rescuer.
items.cn: 短语 thanks to 漂移成因果表达，谢雾与谢救星一样容易。

note.en: The first group is the thank family around the plural; the second sorts the everyday gratitude expressions by tone.
note.cn: 第一组是围绕复数形式的 thank 词族；第二组按语气排列日常感谢用语。

entries.definition: the verb and the rare singular noun; thanks is its plural that ran away
entries.definitionCN: 动词与罕用单数名词；thanks 是跑出去的复数

entries.definition: the adjective of the same family
entries.definitionCN: 同族形容词

entries.definition: the giving of thanks; also the American November holiday
entries.definitionCN: 献上感谢；亦指美国十一月感恩节

entries.definition: the fuller formula, one polite step above thanks
entries.definitionCN: 更完整的套语，比 thanks 客气一档

entries.definition: a casual thanks or toast, common in British speech
entries.definitionCN: 随意致谢或祝酒，英式口语常用

entries.definition: the feeling behind every thanks, named without being spoken
entries.definitionCN: 每声谢谢背后的情感，只命名不说出

normalIntro.en: Real links: the plural shape, give thanks in prayer, thanks to for causes, and the British cheers.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：复数形态、祈祷中的 give thanks、表因果的 thanks to、以及英式 cheers。

normal.en: Thanks is thank made plural: gratitude by the handful.
normal.cn: thanks 是 thank 的复数：一把一把的感激。

normal.en: Give thanks at dinner: the oldest use of the plural.
normal.cn: 饭前 give thanks：复数最古老的用法。

normal.en: Thanks to you, we missed the train; causation with a smile or a frown.
normal.cn: thanks to you 我们误了车；带笑或皱眉的因果。

normal.en: Many thanks sounds heavier than a bare thanks.
normal.cn: many thanks 听起来比光秃秃的 thanks 更重。

normal.en: Cheers, ta, and thanks all live in the same informal street.
normal.cn: cheers、ta 与 thanks 都住在同一条非正式的街上。

abstract.en: A plural for a feeling: gratitude comes in grains, not blocks.
abstract.cn: 给情感配复数：感激是一粒粒来的，不是整块的。

abstract.en: Thanks can be owed before they are spoken.
abstract.cn: 感谢可以欠着，先不说出口。

abstract.en: Some thanks are prayers; some are just small coins dropped in a jar.
abstract.cn: 有的感谢是祈祷；有的只是投进罐里的小硬币。

examples.en: Thanks for the ride, it saved me an hour.
examples.cn: 谢谢捎我一程，省了我一小时。

examples.en: Many thanks to everyone who helped with the move.
examples.cn: 万分感谢帮忙搬家的每一个人。

examples.en: Thanks to the new rule, refunds now arrive in three days.
examples.cn: 多亏新规定，退款三天就能到账。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三克斯」——帮了我三次的人，说三声克斯（thanks）都不够 → thanks 谢谢

root: 古英语 þanc「感念、恩惠」的复数形 → 中古英语口语致谢语 → 现代英语感叹词与复数名词；与 thought 同出日耳曼「思考」词根。

sensesIntro.en: Thanks starts as the plural of gratitude, escapes into speech as the quick exclamation, becomes goodwill that can be sent or owed, and finally stretches into plain causation with thanks to.
sensesIntro.cn: thanks 起于感激的复数，逃进口语成为快捷感叹，成为可寄可欠的善意，最后经 thanks to 拉伸为单纯的因果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gratitude counted in plural, handed over a few grains at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：按复数计数的感激，一次递出几粒。

branches.en: The plural leaves the prayer and enters the street.
branches.cn: 复数离开祈祷，走进街巷。

branches.en: Thanks become coins that can be sent and returned.
branches.cn: 感谢成为可寄可还的硬币。

branches.en: The thanked cause and the plain cause share one phrase.
branches.cn: 被感谢的因与单纯的因共用一个短语。

branches.en: Owing and sending are two directions of the same goodwill.
branches.cn: 亏欠与寄送是同一善意的两个方向。

branches.en: Thanks to the fog: gratitude gone fully grammatical.
branches.cn: thanks to the fog：感激彻底语法化了。

intro.en: Thanks carries the plural -s into compounds and fixed phrases rather than building new words with affixes.
intro.cn: thanks 带着复数 -s 进入复合与固定短语，而不是用词缀另造新词。

latinIntro.en: Thanks is Germanic; Latin gratiae, literally favours in the plural, is the closest parallel and is given as contrast only.
latinIntro.cn: thanks 属日耳曼语源；拉丁 gratiae（字面义复数的「恩惠」）是最接近的平行词，仅作对照。

items.example: Many thanks for your reply.

items.meaning: to express gratitude, especially in prayer
items.example: The family gave thanks before dinner.
Thanks to her, we found the keys.
items.exampleCN: 多亏她，我们找到了钥匙。

items.example: Warm thanks go to the volunteers.
items.exampleCN: 向志愿者们致以诚挚谢意。

items.meaning: to answer a kindness with gratitude
items.example: He returned thanks with a handwritten card.
We won, no thanks to the referee.
items.exampleCN: 我们赢了，可跟裁判没关系。

items.example: The chair proposed a vote of thanks.
items.exampleCN: 主席提议全场鼓掌致谢。

items.example: She wrote a letter of thanks to the hospital.

definition_zh: 那个；那（指示词）；（引导从句）连接词；那样地
definition_en: a demonstrative word pointing at something farther away or already mentioned, also the common linker introducing clauses
core_image: 一根指向稍远处或回指说过之事的手指：既指物，也把句子连起来
scene: 橱窗里有两件毛衣，她指着离自己远的那件。I want that one, the grey sweater in the back row.
sceneCN: 这里 that 是指示词「那个」（第 1 个义项：指向较远或已提及的事物）；句意：我要那个，后排那件灰毛衣。

derivatives.zh: 那些（that 的复数形式）
定冠词（that 的弱化形式，指示义磨损后只保留确定义）
然后；当时（同一指示词家族的时间副词）
比（同族词的分化形，专管比较）

senses.title: Point at something distant or mentioned
senses.definition: used to indicate a person or thing farther away, or already known from earlier talk
senses.definitionCN: 用于指示较远处或前文已提及的人或物
senses.example: Do you remember that summer at the lake?
senses.exampleCN: 还记得湖边那个夏天吗？
senses.why: The finger points away from the speaker's hand, in space or in memory.
senses.whyCN: 这根手指从说话人身边指向远处——或指向空间，或指向记忆。

senses.title: Introduce a clause
senses.definition: a linker introducing noun clauses and certain adverbial clauses, often with little meaning of its own
senses.definitionCN: 引导名词从句及部分状语从句的连接词，自身意义往往很弱
senses.example: She said that the train had left already.
senses.exampleCN: 她说火车已经开走了。
senses.why: The pointing finger goes soft: it no longer points at things but holds a clause onto the verb.
senses.whyCN: 指向的手指软了下来：不再指物，而是把从句扣在动词上。

senses.title: To such a degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective or adverb to mean to that degree, so
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容词或副词前，表示到那种程度
senses.example: I didn't know the exam was that hard.
senses.exampleCN: 我不知道考试有那么难。
senses.why: The pointing power now measures: it points at a degree the listener must fetch from the situation.
senses.whyCN: 指向之力转而量度：指向一个需要听者从情境中取回的程度。

senses.title: Introduce purpose or result
senses.definition: a linker in clauses of purpose or result, as in so that and in order that
senses.definitionCN: 引导目的或结果状语从句，如 so that 与 in order that
senses.example: Speak louder so that everyone can hear.
senses.exampleCN: 大声一点，好让每个人都听见。
senses.why: The same soft linker is trained onto purpose: the clause explains what the action aims at.
senses.whyCN: 同一个软连接词被套上目的：从句解释动作瞄准什么。

intro.en: That is one of the oldest pointing words in English, straight from Old English þæt, the neuter demonstrative. The definite article the, the relatives which and that, and the adverbs then and than all grew from the same demonstrative family.
intro.cn: that 是英语最古老的指向词之一，直接来自古英语中性的指示词 þæt。定冠词 the、关系代词、时间副词 then、比较词 than 都出自同一个指示词家族。

items.en: þæt was the neuter form of the demonstrative family se, seo, þæt, meaning that in the widest sense.
items.cn: þæt 是指示词家族 se、seo、þæt 的中性形式，泛指「那个」。

items.en: The family goes back to a Germanic demonstrative stem that- shared across the old Germanic languages.
items.cn: 该家族可追溯至各古日耳曼语言共享的日耳曼指示词干 that-。

items.en: That took over the relative clause work from older particles, and the that of I think that became a weak syllable.
items.cn: 中古英语中 that 接管了关系从句功能；I think that 中的 that 已是弱音节。

items.en: The demonstrative weakened in unstressed positions and thinned into the article the.
items.cn: 指示词在非重读位置弱化，瘦身为定冠词 the。

items.en: Modern English fixed the plural those, the degree use that hard, and the linker that can even be dropped.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了复数 those、程度用法 that hard；连接词 that 甚至可以省略。

note.en: The first group follows the demonstrative family through its splits; the second compares the pointing words.
note.cn: 第一组沿指示词家族的各支脉追踪；第二组比较各指向词。

entries.definition: the definite article; that worn smooth by constant use
entries.definitionCN: 定冠词；被高频使用磨光滑了的 that

entries.definition: the plural of that for several distant or mentioned things
entries.definitionCN: that 的复数，指多个远处或已提及之物

entries.definition: the comparison word that split off from the same old adverb family
entries.definitionCN: 从同一古老副词家族分化出的比较词

entries.definition: points at what is near the speaker, where that points away
entries.definitionCN: 指向近处；that 指向远处

entries.definition: the other relative word; which follows a comma, that does not in defining clauses
entries.definitionCN: 另一个关系词；限定性从句中 which 前有逗号而 that 无

entries.definition: of the kind just mentioned; points at a kind rather than a single thing
entries.definitionCN: 那样的；指向一类而非单一个体

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Old English þæt, the article the worn out of it, the plural those, and the clause linker that can vanish.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：古英语 þæt、由它磨出的定冠词 the、复数 those、以及可省略的从句连接词 that。

normal.en: That and this point in opposite directions: far and near.
normal.cn: that 与 this 指向相反：远与近。

normal.en: The article the is just that worn down by daily use.
normal.cn: 定冠词 the 就是天天用磨平了的 that。

normal.en: In she said that, the that points at a whole sentence instead of a thing.
normal.cn: 在 she said that 里，that 指向的是整句话而非实物。

normal.en: That hard measures a degree shown by the situation.
normal.cn: that hard 量的是由情境显示出的程度。

normal.en: So that hangs a purpose onto the action.
normal.cn: so that 把目的挂上动作。

abstract.en: Language points twice: once with the finger, once with grammar.
abstract.cn: 语言有两次指向：一次用手，一次用语法。

abstract.en: The busiest word may be the emptiest, only gluing clauses together.
abstract.cn: 最忙的词可能最空，只负责把从句粘住。

abstract.en: Memory is a kind of distance: that summer points as far as any map.
abstract.cn: 记忆也是一种距离：that summer 指得和任何地图一样远。

examples.en: That was the best meal I have had all month.
examples.cn: 那是我这个月吃过最好的一顿饭。

examples.en: He proved that the machine could run without oil.
examples.cn: 他证明了这台机器不用润滑油也能运转。

examples.en: The queue was that long we nearly gave up.
examples.cn: 队伍排得那么长，我们差点放弃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「热特」——手指着远处发烫的东西喊「那个热的」→ that 那个

root: 古英语指示词 þæt（家族 se/seo/þæt 的中性形）→ 日耳曼指示词干 that- → 现代英语 that、those、the、then、than 同族分化。

sensesIntro.en: That begins as the oldest pointing finger of English, weakens into a clause glue, measures degrees, and finally hangs purpose clauses onto actions.
sensesIntro.cn: that 从英语最古老的指向手指出发，弱化为从句粘合剂，转而量度程度，最终把目的从句挂上动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the old finger of English, pointing far, then pointing at nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：英语古老的手指，先指远处，后什么都不指。

branches.en: The finger in space and in memory.
branches.cn: 空间与记忆中的手指。

branches.en: The finger goes soft and holds clauses on verbs.
branches.cn: 手指变软，扣住动词上的从句。

branches.en: The finger measures a degree instead of a place.
branches.cn: 手指不再量位置而量程度。

branches.en: The finger aims the clause at a purpose.
branches.cn: 手指把从句瞄准目的。

branches.en: Pointing at things and holding sentences are one gesture worn differently.
branches.cn: 指物与粘句是同一手势的不同磨损。

intro.en: That has no affixes; its family is made of other words grown from the same Germanic pointing stem.
intro.cn: that 没有词缀；它的家族是从同一日耳曼指向词干长出的其他词。

latinIntro.en: That is Germanic; Latin demonstratives are given only as contrast.
latinIntro.cn: that 属日耳曼语源；拉丁指示词仅作对照。

items.meaning: that; the neuter of se, seo, þæt
items.example: þæt is the direct source of that.
items.exampleCN: þæt 是 that 的直接来源。

items.example: Those apples are sour.
The sun rises early here.

items.meaning: in order to; with the result that
items.example: Save now so that you can rest later.
items.exampleCN: 现在攒钱，日后才歇得安心。

items.example: Now that you are here, we can start.
items.exampleCN: 既然你来了，我们可以开始了。

items.example: He is frugal, that is to say, very careful with money.
items.exampleCN: 他很节俭，也就是说花钱极为谨慎。

items.example: I cannot eat that much.
You may go, provided that you return by six.
items.exampleCN: 你可以去，只要六点前回来。

latinEntries.meaning: that; the far-pointing word of Latin
which; who; the clause linker of Latin
latinEntries.meaningCN: 关系词；拉丁语的从句连接词

definition_zh: 定冠词：这；那（用于特指已知事物）；也用于独一无二之物
definition_en: the definite article, marking a noun as particular and already known, or unique in its kind
core_image: 谈话双方共知的一件东西被轻轻一指：别找错了，就是这一个
scene: 办公室里只有一台咖啡机，人人都懂。Please refill the coffee machine before it runs dry.
sceneCN: 这里 the 是定冠词（第 1 个义项：特指双方已知之物）；句意：请在咖啡机用干前把它加满。

pos.zh: 定冠词：特指；已知；独一无二

collocations.zh: 美国（复数国名前加 the）

derivatives.zh: 那个（the 的完整指示祖先，指示义保留）
这个（同族近指词）
那些（that 的复数）

senses.title: Mark a particular known thing
senses.definition: marks a noun as one that the listener can identify from context or shared knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 标示名词为听者可凭上下文或共有知识识别的特定之物
senses.example: Close the door, please, the one you just came through.
senses.exampleCN: 请关门，就是你刚进来的那扇。
senses.why: The article does the pointing without a finger: shared knowledge does the aiming.
senses.whyCN: 冠词不用手指就完成指向：瞄准的是双方共有的知识。

senses.title: Mark what is unique of its kind
senses.definition: used before nouns whose referent is unique, like the sun, the moon, the sea
senses.definitionCN: 用于所指独一无二的名词前，如 the sun、the moon、the sea
senses.example: The moon was bright enough to read by.
senses.exampleCN: 月亮亮得都能借着看书。
senses.why: When there is only one, no pointing is needed: uniqueness does the work of the finger.
senses.whyCN: 只有一物时无需指向：独一无二本身就是手指。

senses.title: Turn an adjective or a family name into a group
senses.titleCN: 使形容词或姓氏变为全体
senses.definition: turns an adjective into a noun phrase for a whole class, as in the rich, and marks family names in the plural, as in the Smiths
senses.definitionCN: 把形容词变成指全类的名词短语（如 the rich），也用于复数姓氏（如 the Smiths）
senses.example: The rich are not always happier than the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 富人并不总比穷人快乐。
senses.why: One word turns a quality into all the people who carry it.
senses.whyCN: 一个词把一种品质变成所有携带它的人。

senses.title: Used with comparatives for proportion
senses.definition: used before comparatives in the pattern the more, the better to link two changing quantities
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the more, the better 格式中，连接两个联动变化的量
senses.example: The sooner we leave, the cheaper the tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 走得越早，票价越便宜。
senses.why: Two weak thes become two pans of a scale that move together.
senses.whyCN: 两个弱化的 the 变成联动天平的两只秤盘。

intro.en: The is that worn thin. It comes from the same Old English demonstrative se, seo, þæt; in unstressed speech the pointing meaning sanded away, leaving only certainty.
intro.cn: the 是被磨薄的 that。它出自同一个古英语指示词家族 se、seo、þæt；在轻读语音中指向义被磨掉，只剩下确定性。

items.en: The demonstrative family se, seo, þæt declined fully, and se served as the ordinary marker of known things.
items.cn: 指示词家族 se、seo、þæt 有完整变格，se 充当已知事物的普通标记。

items.en: In weak positions the word shortened and lost its stress and much of its pointing force.
items.cn: 在弱读位置上，该词缩短，失去重音与大部分指向力。

items.en: The family descends from a Germanic demonstrative stem shared with that, this, those, then and than.
items.cn: 该家族出自与 that、this、those、then、than 共享的日耳曼指示词干。

items.en: Middle English fixed the as the all-purpose definite article, using it where Latin would use nothing at all.
items.cn: 中古英语把 the 定为通用定冠词，用在拉丁语根本不加词的位置。

items.en: Modern English extended it to unique things, classes of people, and the proportional the more, the better.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到独一之物、人群类别与比例式的 the more, the better。

note.en: The first group is the demonstrative family that the article came from; the second contrasts article systems.
note.cn: 第一组是定冠词所出自的指示词家族；第二组对比冠词体系。

entries.definition: the demonstrative that the article was ground down from
entries.definitionCN: 定冠词由它磨出的指示词

entries.definition: the near-pointing member of the same demonstrative family
entries.definitionCN: 同一指示词家族的近指成员

entries.definition: the time adverb of the same old pointing word
entries.definitionCN: 同一古老指向词的时间副词支脉

entries.definition: the indefinite article for things not yet identified
entries.definitionCN: 不定冠词，用于尚未确定之物

entries.definition: the indefinite article before vowels
entries.definitionCN: 元音前的不定冠词

entries.definition: the neuter demonstrative of Old English, the article's full-bodied ancestor
entries.definitionCN: 古英语中性指示词，定冠词饱满的祖先

normalIntro.en: Real links: the demonstrative ancestor, the unique sun and moon, the rich as a class, and the piano rule.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：指示词祖先、独一的日月、作为类别的 the rich、乐器加 the 的规则。

normal.en: The is that with the pointing filed off.
normal.cn: the 是把指向锉掉的 that。

normal.en: The sun and the moon need no finger: there is only one of each.
normal.cn: the sun 与 the moon 无需手指：各自只有一个。

normal.en: The rich means all the people who are rich.
normal.cn: the rich 指所有富有的人。

normal.en: The more, the better: two thes pull the scale together.
normal.cn: the more, the better：两个 the 把天平联起来。

normal.en: Play the piano, not a piano: instruments take the definite article.
normal.cn: play the piano 而非 a piano：乐器前用定冠词。

abstract.en: Certainty is the residue of pointing.
abstract.cn: 确定性是指向磨剩的渣。

abstract.en: A word can fade until only its grammar is left.
abstract.cn: 词可以淡到只剩下语法。

abstract.en: The smallest English word carries the heaviest job: deciding what both speakers already know.
abstract.cn: 英语最小的词扛着最重的活：判定双方已共知什么。

examples.en: The book you lent me changed how I cook.
examples.cn: 你借我的那本书改变了我的做菜方式。

examples.en: The sea was calm at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时海面很平静。

examples.en: The older we grow, the faster the years seem to pass.
examples.cn: 年纪越大，岁月似乎过得越快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「热」——聊起来双方心里都热的那件东西，不用说清也指得到 → the 定冠词

root: 古英语指示词 se/seo/þæt（日耳曼指示词干）弱读磨损 → 中古英语定冠词 the；与 that、this、those、then、than 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The begins as a worn-out demonstrative, keeps certainty without pointing, and expands to unique things, whole classes and linked proportions.
sensesIntro.cn: the 起于磨损的指示词，留住不指向的确定性，再扩展到独一之物、整个类别与联动比例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger sanded down to certainty only.
core.cn: 核心意象：被磨得只剩确定性的手指。

branches.en: Shared knowledge aims the word where a finger would.
branches.cn: 共有知识替手指完成瞄准。

branches.en: Uniqueness points by itself.
branches.cn: 独一无二自己就会指向。

branches.en: Classes and proportions show the article building bigger things.
branches.cn: 类别与比例显示冠词搭建更大的结构。

branches.en: Known and unique both spare the speaker a real gesture.
branches.cn: 已知与独一都让说话者省去真实的手势。

branches.en: One article turns an adjective into a crowd.
branches.cn: 一个冠词把形容词变成人群。

intro.en: The has no affixes at all; it is pure grammar, and its family is the Germanic demonstrative group.
intro.cn: the 完全没有词缀；它是纯粹的语法词，家族即日耳曼指示词群。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no definite article; the demonstratives listed here are contrast only.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有定冠词；所列指示词仅作对照。

items.meaning: the source family of the, that, this
items.example: Middle English speakers wore se down into the.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语说话者把 se 磨成了 the。

items.meaning: the more one thing grows, the more another follows
items.example: The faster you drive, the more fuel you burn.
The young understand the web better.
We took the same train.
The Philippines lie east of Vietnam.
She plays the violin in the band.
The parking lot charges by the hour.
I saw her the other day at the market.
items.exampleCN: 前几天我在市场见过她。

latinEntries.meaning: this; the near demonstrative of Latin
that; the far demonstrative of Latin

definition_zh: 剧院；戏院；戏剧；手术室（英式旧用）
